name: manual_32441b
claim: On Windows, a script that must call another PowerShell script as a real separate process (not in-process) needs 'powershell.exe -File <script>', not the venv's python.exe — passing a .ps1 to python.exe is a silent no-op, not an error.

decisions.notes: install.ps1 called '& $VenvPython (Join-Path $ScriptDir start.ps1) --discover' to regenerate .paths.ps1 as a separate process (needed because that nested call does exit 0, which would kill the parent process if run in-process via &). Passing a .ps1 file to python.exe doesn't throw — it just doesn't do anything meaningful, so the bug was invisible until the actual downstream effect (.paths.ps1 never written) was checked. Fixed by invoking powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File explicitly.
